claim: Own-name noticing in shadowing is real but a minority result: about 29-35% of shadowers report their own name in the unattended ear (Moray 33%, Wood and Cowan 34.6%, Roer and Cowan 29% with N=80). About two thirds never notice.
agent_test: Not an agent test. Use as a prior that unattended content is rarely processed.
audit_note: Roer & Cowan 2021: 29% of N=80 reported own name, described as a minority result; Conway et al. 2001 gives Moray 33% and Wood & Cowan 34.6%; Roer & Cowan text rounds Wood & Cowan to 35%.

claim: Working-memory span moderates own-name noticing in the original (20% high span vs 65% low span, N=40), but the preregistered replication gave inconclusive Bayes factors (BF10 0.58 to 1.02), so the span link is contested.
agent_test: None needed. Do not build a rule on span-dependent leakage.

claim: Own-name capture is a short, local cost: shadowing errors rise at the name and the next two words, not before or three words later; in a categorisation task the name slowed responses by over 100 ms (N=37) and the effect shrank as speech was compressed.
agent_test: Insert a salient, self-relevant but irrelevant token (the task name) into context and measure accuracy at equal tokens.
audit_note: Roer & Cowan 2021: shadowing errors rise at the name and the next two words, none before or three words after (Bayes factors); Li et al. 2024 Exp 1: final N=37 (39 tested), own name over 100 ms slower, capture weakened with compression (none at 25%); 'effect shrank' is for Exp 2 with 25 per level.

claim: Perceptual-load theory (less distraction under high load) is weakly supported by recent work: Snowden and Gray 2025 found distraction largely independent of load across six experiments, Marciano and Yeshurun found large individual and within-person variation, and dilution accounts explain many load effects.
agent_test: None. Do not use perceptual load as an agent design principle.

claim: Load-induced inattentional blindness exists: at high load, detection of an unexpected cross fell to 37% from 90% at low load (Macdonald and Lavie 2008, N=16).
agent_test: Not testable directly on LLMs.

claim: Neural evidence is mixed on whether unattended speech is linguistically processed: some frontal tracking of unattended structure (n=29 and n=23, p near .045) but brainstem responses show moderate evidence against attention effects. Small samples.
agent_test: None.

claim: LLMs are easily distracted by irrelevant context: on GSM-IC, no more than 18% of baseline-solved problems stay solved across all distractor types, and macro accuracy is below 30% for code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. All four lines come from one paper. 2025 update: reasoning models (R1, R1-distill, QwQ, o1, o3-mini) are also distracted by irrelevant trigger sentences (R1 combined attack success 4.50% vs 1.50% random; up to 3x longer answers).
agent_test: Rerun GSM-IC style distractors on the current model with and without a filter step at equal total tokens.

claim: Sampling helps against distraction: self-consistency with 20 samples adds more than 11 points micro accuracy (35.5 for 0-COT) and the right answer is among the samples 99.7% of the time, but best macro accuracy is still only 45%.
agent_test: Compare vote-over-N against a rewrite-then-solve filter at equal tokens.

claim: Rewriting the context to remove irrelevant or opinion text before answering (System 2 Attention, a hard filter) beats prompting to ignore it: factual QA 62.8 to 80.3% (oracle 82.0), instruction-only 71.7%, keep-original 74.5%; GSM-IC in-topic 51.7 to 61.3%. One paper, LLaMA-2-70B-chat only.
agent_test: Implement a filter-rewrite operator and test on distractor QA at equal tokens, counting the extra rewrite pass.

claim: Telling a model to ignore irrelevant text helps little compared with removing it; instructions with original exemplars can match uninstructed distractor exemplars.
agent_test: Instruction-only arm versus filter arm at equal tokens.

claim: Long-context position effect: accuracy is U-shaped over document position; GPT-3.5 at 20 and 30 documents fell below closed-book 56.1%; more than 20 retrieved documents added only 1.5% (GPT-3.5) and 1% (Claude-1.3). 2025 update: the middle dip is strongest only up to about half of the context window and fades beyond, where an end-proximity bias dominates (Veseli et al.); Chroma found no needle position effect in 18 models.
agent_test: Place key evidence first or last and truncate the rest; measure at equal tokens. Models are 2023 vintage.

claim: Architecture-level selective attention cuts the cost of unneeded context: Selective Attention matches transformers with 2x heads; 16x, 25x, 47x less attention memory only with an extra memory loss (5x, 7x, 8x with standard loss). Differential Transformer reports up to 30 points better multi-needle retrieval at N=6, R=2. Both are training changes, outside our scaffold.
agent_test: Not testable by scaffold. Background only.
audit_note: Minor: 30 points is stated as 30% accuracy gap in the paper; 5x/7x/8x with standard loss confirmed in Sec 6.2 of Selective Attention PDF.

claim: More irrelevant context steadily lowers multi-step reasoning accuracy: at depth 5 Grok-3-Beta step accuracy fell from 43% (1 distractor) to 19% (15), and GPT-4.1 from 26% to 2%.
agent_test: Scale distractor count and measure the accuracy slope with and without a filter.
audit_note: Numbers appear only in the GSM-DC paper (listed twice); Shi 2023 supports the general distraction claim.

claim: Audio-language models fail cocktail-party selection: at 0 dB open models pick the distractor stream on 21.5-41.0% of items; Gemini-2.0-Flash drops from 0.955 single-stream to 0.242 cocktail party. Human and model selective-attention gaps differ by language. Gap check: 0.320 is Gemini-2.0-Flash with a Spanish distractor at +5 dB; the same-language cell equals the single-stream 0.955 (possible table slip).
agent_test: Not applicable to a text agent.
audit_note: All MUSI numbers match (Tables 2, 7, 11); the 0.320 cell is English target with Spanish distractor; MUSI listed several times is one paper.

claim: No LLM or AI study in the set tests Broadbent, Treisman or Deutsch and Deutsch directly; a full-text grep of four main papers found zero mentions. The link is analogy only.
agent_test: None.

claim: Conflict and Stroop-style effects appear in LLMs and VLMs (Gemma-2-2B congruent 0.9644 vs incongruent 0.5676 delta probability; CLIP ink accuracy 15.9%), suggesting competition between relevant and irrelevant features inside models.
agent_test: Probe only if we need mechanism. Not a scaffold lever.

claim: Reasoning models are still distracted by irrelevant text. Appending a trivia sentence, a savings statement or a misleading numeric hint raised DeepSeek R1 attack success from 1.50% (random) to 4.50% and R1-distill-Qwen-32B to 8.00%, and slowed answers to 1.5x token budget in 26.4% (o1), 16.8% (o3-mini), 28.0% (R1) and 42.2% (R1-distill) of cases. The absolute rate is small and the triggers were adversarially searched.
agent_test: Run GSM-IC style distractors on our agent's reasoning model; compare plain vs ignore-instruction vs rewrite at equal tokens.

claim: A plain 'ignore irrelevant statements' instruction cut Llama-3.1-8B attack success from 37.5% to 9.9% on CatAttack triggers. This contrasts with Weston and Sukhbaatar, where instructions helped little; the two used different models and distractor types.
agent_test: A/B an ignore line against an S2A rewrite on the same distractor set.

claim: Input length hurts even with perfect retrieval and even when the padding is whitespace or masked (13.9% to 85% drops; Llama3 VarSum 96.0 to 11 at 30,000 masked tokens). A recite-the-evidence-first step recovers much of it for a 7B model (up to +31.2 points) and little for GPT-4o (up to +4.0 on RULER QA2).
agent_test: Compare full history vs recited or truncated history at equal tokens on our long tasks.

claim: Coherent haystack text is more distracting than shuffled text across all 18 tested 2025 models, and focused short prompts beat full-history prompts (113k vs 300 tokens) for every model on LongMemEval. Source is a vendor report, not peer reviewed.
agent_test: Replicate the focused vs full contrast with our own memory store.

claim: Original Moray (1959), Treisman (1960) and Treisman and Geffen (1967) numbers could not be read this session (paywalls, search budget). Only Moray 33% and Wood and Cowan 34.6% are available second-hand; the '4 of 12' detail for Moray is unverified.
agent_test: None; obtain originals through a library.

claim: No independent replication of Snowden and Gray's load-independence was found. 2026 load studies (Wang and Chen) show load effects reverse with spatial layout, so load theory stays contested.
agent_test: None.

claim: No study was found comparing an S2A-style rewrite with best-of-N or self-consistency at equal total tokens on distractor QA.
agent_test: Own bench: S2A rewrite vs best-of-N, equal tokens, GSM-IC with a reasoning model.
